comment: D’s Adam 1e-4 beat E’s AdamW 1e-3 despite identical architectures and tenfold nominal progress. I missed a recipe-specific test-CE reversal: faster fitting may worsen held-out confidence, but ordinal results cannot distinguish this from optimization instability or decay effects. K1001/K1012 warned against maximizing displacement; I underweighted that warning. K1002 helped rank the slow Adagrad choices. Backtesting found no matching historical rate twins; the sole mixed-architecture historical 1e-4-versus-1e-3 comparison favored the higher rate. Matched lab comparisons likewise favored higher Adam-family rates in 14/14 pairs across three datasets, with repeated controls. Thus a general “lower rate wins XOR” rule is unsupported; this wide, batch-64, 512-step recipe needs targeted validation.
